rendered: The review cites a froth flotation study in which the collector was kerosene[1]. In that study, the share of graphite that floated was over 90% of spent graphite[2], which is hydrophobic, and it floated in the froth layers. The cathode tailing product reached 88.2% active cathode materials[3] (purity), at a recovery of 74.3%[4] total recovery, which the review credits to the effectiveness of the froth flotation process for purification.
